heard: A spacecraft designed to die in 32 minutes lasted two hours. On March 1, 1982, the Soviet Union's Venera 13 lander descended through the clouds of Venus. The probe touched down near Phoebe-Rigio, facing 90 atmospheres of pressure and temperatures around 460 degrees Celsius. Safe inside its armored hull, Venera 13 drilled into the rocky ground to analyze a soil sample. It also captured and transmitted the first color photographs ever taken from the surface of another planet. Decades later, a Russian scientist claimed these photos showed moving alien life, like a scorpion. But experts proved the mysterious alien was actually just the lander's discarded camera lens cap. In 1982, Soviet engineers celebrated as this historic machine defied its death sentence on Venus.
